Independently re-derived. יֹֽאמַר נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל is byte-identical to Ps.124.1's closing title clause -- a legitimate intertextual echo, correctly disclosed as texture and correctly not used to argue a cross-psalm merge. The 129.1/129.2 repeated line is confirmed a genuine skeleton-tier match (רבת צררוני מנעורי, 3 of 3 words) differing only in the final word's vowel suffix at the byte tier, exactly as claimed. The 129:3 ketiv/qere pair (למענותם / לְמַעֲנִיתָֽם) is confirmed present inline in the staged source text in that order (the INLINE-KETIV hazard pattern), and pmarks_Ps.json's kq inventory confirms Ps.129.3 carries exactly 1 K/Q note -- correctly disclosed. check_tiling.py confirms exact 1-8 coverage. The whole-psalm verdict itself is sound. However the rationale's claim that 'no further address or topic shift interrupts the movement from affliction to curse across the remaining six verses' is a universal absence-claim carrying no adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its unit, flagged by check_universals.py. On independent re-derivation the substance holds (no new named party enters vv3-8; 'the wicked' at v4 and 'those who hate Zion' at v5 read as the same opposing party under different epithets, not a fresh addressee), so this does not change the verdict -- but it is a real evidence-discipline gap against the standing rule that every universal claim ships with an adjacent digit-bearing sweep, a rule the cluster's own sibling row (M8-Ps-434) satisfies correctly for an analogous claim.

This is the strongest-evidenced split in the cluster (an objective named-party sweep rather than a softer topical read); the row's medium confidence is defensible but conservative relative to that crispness -- an observation, not a defect, since split-vs-whole-psalm decisions carry inherent structural uncertainty this campaign treats uniformly across the cluster. No defect found.
